title: Page keys bypass the one keymap: scoped bindings the conflict report sees
acceptance: conflictReport(KEYMAP).shadows -> lists exactly: review.player shadows global 1-7 (page jump) and ArrowLeft/ArrowRight in l2; characters.roster shadows ArrowLeft/ArrowRight (page-step) in l1 - today the report has no shadows field and cannot see either

body:
## Summary
The console's keyboard has a registry that claims to be the only one (keymap.ts:1-2, keyCommands.ts:1-3) and a conflict report that proves nothing collides - but the two densest keyboard surfaces, the review player and the character roster, bind keys in private onKeyDown handlers that shadow the global 1-7 page jumps and arrow page-steps by calling preventDefault first. The report cannot see them, the player carries a second typing rule, and 'r' is swallowed on every layer-2 page though only Brain owns it. Give bindings a focus scope, resolve innermost-scope-first in the one listener, and make the report list scope shadows as owner-visible facts.

## Description
Leans on accessibility / keyboard-navigation-models ('Shortcuts are accelerators... Discoverable somewhere structural... Never steal typing' - one typing rule, one reference surface) and app-shell / shell-hosted-services (the chord engine is a shell resident; pages declare, the shell resolves). Today a page that wants keys must re-implement the listener (Player.tsx:93-109) and rely on React's bubbling order to beat the window listener; the keymap's guarantees stop at the shell's own bindings.

The move: `Binding.scope?: KeyScope` (typed union in keys/scopes.ts: 'review.player' | 'characters.roster'), scoped actions `{type:'scoped', scope, command, arg?}`, and a `data-key-scope` attribute on the owning element. listener.ts resolves by walking `e.target.closest('[data-key-scope]')` innermost-first, then global; a command binding resolves only when an owner is mounted, so an unowned 'r' falls through un-prevented. kit/keyCommands.ts generalises useKeyCommand into `useKeyScope(scope, handlers)` typed by the scope's command map; the duplicate KeyCommand goes. conflictReport gains `shadows: {scope, mode, chord, global, scoped}[]`, pinned by test the way meaningChanges is. KEYMAP page bindings come from PAGE_IDS. Player and roster delete their onKeyDown and the private typing().

## Flow
- keys/scopes.ts: KeyScope union, per-scope command maps, scopeChain(target)
- keymap.ts: scoped bindings for review.player (1-8 toggle, Enter save, Ctrl+Enter save typing:'only', arrows) and characters.roster (arrows); page bindings from PAGE_IDS
- listener.ts: resolve(keymap, mode, chord, typing, scopes, owned) innermost-first; one isTypingTarget
- conflicts.ts: per-scope conflicts + shadows
- Shell.tsx / keyActions.ts: route scoped effects to useKeyScope owners; ownership check before preventDefault
- Player.tsx, characters/Layer1.tsx: data-key-scope + useKeyScope, onKeyDown deleted

## Expected impact
Every key the operator can press is in one table the report checks: the next page that adds keys (On Air replay, Simulator) cannot silently steal 1-7, and the shortcut help surface the Binding.label field already anticipates (keymap.ts:35) becomes derivable instead of hand prose. Removes a second typing rule and the dead-'r' swallow.

## Evaluation
Claim: page-local key handling becomes declared, conflict-checked registry entries with identical operator behaviour.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no shadows field; no scope resolution; 'r' prevented with no owner; Player keeps private typing(); PAGE_COUNT literal; onKeyDown in both pages)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first in keymap.test.ts, player.test.tsx, layer1.test.tsx; existing player/roster/shell/preflight suites stay green as the behaviour-preservation check
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence: keys/keymap.ts:1 '// The one keymap registry. Every global key binding the console has is declared here, per mode,'; kit/keyCommands.ts:3 'never listen to the keyboard themselves'; pages/review/Player.tsx:102 'if (/^[1-8]$/.test(e.key)) panel.current?.toggle(Number(e.key) - 1);' :107 '// Consumed: the shell's keymap (bare 1-7 jump pages) skips a prevented event.'; pages/characters/Layer1.tsx:142 '// The roster owns its arrows; the keymap leaves a handled key alone.'; keymap.ts:41 'const PAGE_COUNT = 7;'; keymap.ts:22 and keyCommands.ts:7 'export type KeyCommand = "rerun";'; grep useKeyCommand -> only pages/brain/Preflight.tsx:75; grep onKeyDown apps/console/src/pages -> characters/Layer1.tsx:140, review/FeedbackPanel.tsx:70, review/Player.tsx:93; grep 'addEventListener("keydown' -> only keys/listener.ts:29.

critic.reason: Sound architecture move; one acceptance case is unfalsifiable as written.

revision: Rewrite case 5 with observable outcomes: keydown '1' with focus on a checkbox inside the review player -> mark 1 toggles; keydown '1' with focus on the player's <video> -> no mark toggles and route unchanged; keydown '1' in a text <input> -> nothing fires.

title: Every query region says how old its data is when the live feed can't vouch
shared_surfaces: apps/console/src/data (console-data-layer context, coupled): Query<T> gains updatedAt; the stream-reopen hook revalidates watched ready entries
acceptance: QueryView with data fetched at 14:02:31, stream 'open', no issue -> no freshness line rendered (live path adds zero nodes; shell DOM-count test unchanged)
same data, stream 'reconnecting' (summary degraded) -> line 'As of 14:02:31 · live updates paused' with a Refresh button that calls query.reload; role=status
failed refresh over held data (errorView set) -> degraded panel title carries the time: 'Showing the reply from 14:02:31 · <title>' instead of the timeless 'Showing the last good reply'
query.refreshing true over held data -> region aria-busy='true', content still rendered, no placeholder
cache: entry ready at t0, stream closes, reopens at t1 -> watched ready entries refetch once (today only status 'error' entries retry); unwatched entries are not fetched
freshnessOf: updatedAt undefined -> 'none'; stream open but updatedAt older than the last reopen -> 'unconfirmed' until the refetch lands, then 'live'
Preflight renders 'Last run hh:mm:ss' from query.updatedAt; grep 'layer.cache.getSnapshot' apps/console/src/pages -> 0 hits
premise: apps/console/src/kit/QueryView.tsx:16-33 - with data present QueryView renders children with no age and no refreshing signal; :25 the failed-refresh panel says 'Showing the last good reply' without saying from when
apps/console/src/data/cache.ts:16 - QuerySnapshot.updatedAt exists; apps/console/src/data/react.tsx:29-37 - Query<T> drops it
apps/console/src/pages/brain/Preflight.tsx:71-73 - Brain reaches around the hook into layer.cache.getSnapshot(queryKey(...)).updatedAt because Query hides the time
apps/console/src/data/cache.ts:1-3,40 - freshness is event invalidation plus a 5-minute backstop; while /events is down nothing invalidates

apps/console/src/data/layer.ts:91-93 and apps/console/src/data/cache.ts:110-113 - on stream reopen only entries in status 'error' refetch; ready entries that missed events during the gap stay stale up to 5 min while the chip reads 'online'

apps/console/src/kit/QueryView.tsx:46-53 - ConnectionState is the only feed-aware wrapper and it replaces content; used in 2 page files (pages/reconcile/ChatPage.tsx:53, pages/reconcile/NoReport.tsx:37) against 37 <QueryView> uses in 29 page files
apps/console/src/shell/Chrome.tsx:13-17 - the only freshness signal is one global connection chip; nothing ties it to the region the operator is reading
rollback: Two commits: (1) data layer exposes updatedAt + revalidate-on-reopen, (2) QueryView freshness line + Preflight cleanup; reverting (2) leaves an unused field, reverting (1) restores today's reopen behaviour.
test_command: pnpm -C apps/console test -- kit/queryView data/cache pages/brain app/shell && pnpm -C apps/console typecheck && pnpm -C apps/console lint && pnpm -C apps/console build
runner_up: Shortcut reference overlay ('?' in every mode) rendered from KEYMAP labels plus the live page's owned commands, replacing the hand prose key list in ReviewByType.tsx:38-39 - strongest once card A lands scopes.
body:
## Summary
The operator reads run tables, verdicts and rundowns through one primitive, QueryView, that never says how old the numbers are. Freshness rides on /events invalidation; when the feed drops, every region keeps showing its last reply as if live, and after the feed reopens the ready entries are not revalidated at all - they wait for the 5-minute backstop while the chip says 'online'. The app holds the timestamp (cache.ts:16) and the connection state; QueryView should spend them: an 'As of 14:02:31 · live updates paused · Refresh' line exactly when the feed cannot vouch for the region, a timed failed-refresh banner, and an ambient busy state.

## Description
Leans on async-ui-states / failure-states ('a failed refresh keeps the content on screen... ideally with how stale the data now is... showing old data as if fresh is its own small lie', failure-states.md:62-68), the golden path's `refreshing` row (existing content with at most an ambient indicator), and client-fetch-cache / swr-design (a backstop is not the primary freshness mechanism). A pure `freshnessOf(snapshot, connection, lastReopenAt)` returns live | unconfirmed | failed | none; QueryView renders a one-line Freshness strip only for unconfirmed/failed, so the live path adds no nodes and no per-tick work (absolute time, no ticking clock - cache.ts:3 'No per-tick work'). The coupled data-layer change is two small edits: Query<T> carries updatedAt, and the stream-reopen hook revalidates watched ready entries (not just failed ones) so the strip clears itself honestly.

## Flow
- data/react.tsx: Query.updatedAt
- data/cache.ts: revalidateWatched(); data/layer.ts: call it on reopen after a gap and record lastReopenAt
- kit/freshness.ts: pure classifier (tested without DOM)
- kit/Freshness.tsx: role=status line + Refresh; QueryView sets aria-busy while refreshing
- Preflight.tsx: read query.updatedAt, drop the cache reach-around

## Expected impact
37 query regions across all seven pages gain an honest staleness statement by construction; the operator stops acting on minutes-old rundown or verdict numbers during a feed gap, and stale-after-reconnect drops from up to 5 minutes to one round-trip.

## Evaluation
Claim: regions the live feed cannot vouch for say so and offer a refresh; reconnect revalidates.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no strip, timeless degraded title, no aria-busy, reopen retries only errors, no classifier, Preflight reaches into the cache)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first (kit/queryView.dom.test.tsx, data/cache.test.ts); shell DOM-count test proves the live path adds no nodes
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: kit/QueryView.tsx:25 'title={`Showing the last good reply · ${query.errorView.title}`}'; data/cache.ts:16 'readonly updatedAt: number | undefined;'; data/react.tsx:29-37 Query has status,data,error,errorView,refreshing,reload - no updatedAt; pages/brain/Preflight.tsx:73 'const at = layer.cache.getSnapshot(queryKey("preflight.run", PREFLIGHT_PARAMS)).updatedAt;'; data/layer.ts:91-92 'if (status === "open") { if (everOpened) cache.retryFailed();'; data/cache.ts:112 'if (e.snapshot.status === "error" && e.listeners.size > 0 && !e.inflight)'; data/cache.ts:40 'DEFAULT_BACKSTOP_MS = 5 * 60_000'; grep '<QueryView' apps/console/src/pages -> 37 hits in 29 files; grep ConnectionState apps/console/src/pages -> reconcile/ChatPage.tsx, reconcile/NoReport.tsx only.

critic.reason: Grounded and useful; one case is green before the build.

revision: Drop acceptance case 1 (already passes today; keep it only as a regression assertion inside the existing shell DOM-count test, not as an acceptance case).
